title: Northern Circuit: The Longest Route on Kilimanjaro
excerpt: The Northern Circuit is the longest route on Kilimanjaro, nine days around the quiet north side. It has the best acclimatisation profile of all routes.
body:
The Northern Circuit is the newest and longest route on Kilimanjaro. It starts like Lemosho on the western side, but instead of heading to the busy southern circuit, it curves around the quiet northern slopes before the summit attempt.

## Why nine days matters

The longer you take, the more time your body has to adapt to thinner air. That is why the Northern Circuit is generally seen as the route with the highest chance of reaching Uhuru Peak. It is also the quietest: for several days you may see only your own crew.

## The route in outline

- Days 1–3: Londorossi Gate, forest, Shira Plateau (shared with Lemosho).
- Day 4: Lava Tower for acclimatisation, then north instead of south.
- Days 5–7: around the northern slopes via Buffalo, Third Cave and School Hut, with views over the plains towards Kenya.
- Day 8: summit night via Gilman's Point to Uhuru Peak, descent on the south side.
- Day 9: down to Mweka Gate.

## Who it suits

- People who want the best acclimatisation.
- Travellers who enjoy long walks and solitude.
- Anyone who wants to see a side of Kilimanjaro few people see.

## What to consider

Nine days on the mountain is a real commitment. You are camping all the way, and the price is higher than a shorter route because of park fees and crew days. Ask us [what makes up the cost of a climb](/blog/kilimanjaro-cost-explained/).

If nine days is too long, [Lemosho in eight days](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/) is the closest alternative. [Plan your climb with us](/travel-proposal/).
